newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-CBA-HK Bank in $250 mln wool credit for China.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-CBA-HK Bank in $250 mln wool credit for China.

text.p: The Commonwealth Bank of Australia said it and HSBC Holdings Plc unit HongkongBank of Australia Ltd would underwrite a US$250 million revolving credit facility for Chinese importers of Australian wool.

"The loan facilities offer Chinese importers a new financing structure, jointly underwritten by the Commonwealth Bank and HongKongBank of Australia, secured by documentary credits issued by selected Chinese banks," Commonwealth Bank said in a statement.
The facility would significantly reduce the cost of funding wool imports into China, the bank said.

Australian wool exporters previously arranged funding but many were hit in recent years when Chinese importers reneged on contracts after Chinese customs began enforcing raw wool import tariffs or the market moved against the importers.

"By working directly with selected major wool importers, we believe the facility will encourage more regular and stable buying and will build confidence among Australian wool exporters," the bank said.
China is Australia's biggest single wool customer.
Provisional data shows it imported 161 million kg of Australian wool in the 1995/96 season ended June 30, out of total Australian exports of 794 million kg greasy equivalent.
